# 1. Purpose of the experiment

This experiment asks when modern tree-based machine-learning methods begin to
outperform forecasting approaches that resemble the information environment of
the earlier M competitions.

The comparison starts with information derived only from a store's own sales
history. It then adds information in stages:

1. origin-safe sales-history features;
2. calendar information;
3. store and competition attributes;
4. promotion and holiday information.

The same stores, training period, 42-day fixed-origin test period, model
settings, and evaluation metrics are retained at every stage. Consequently,
changes in performance can be attributed to the newly available information
rather than to a different sample or forecast horizon.

Unlike a rolling one-day-ahead design, no realised sales from the 42-day test
period are used to construct predictors. The shortest sales lag is therefore
42 calendar days. This makes every feature available at the common forecast
origin.

# 2. Packages and configuration

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(zoo)
library(xgboost)
library(lightgbm)
library(forecast)

DATA_DIR <- "/home/whu/isik.kayra/projects"
TRAIN_CSV <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "train.csv")
STORE_CSV <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "store.csv")

OUTPUT_DIR <- "old_m_to_modern_ml_outputs"
dir.create(OUTPUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

TEST_DAYS <- 42L
CV_FOLDS <- 3L
XGB_MAX_ROUNDS <- 300L
LGB_MAX_ROUNDS <- 1000L
XGB_EARLY_STOP <- 20L
LGB_EARLY_STOP <- 40L
DETECTED_CORES <- parallel::detectCores()
if (is.na(DETECTED_CORES)) DETECTED_CORES <- 2L
N_THREADS <- max(1L, DETECTED_CORES - 1L)
STAT_WORKERS <- min(8L, N_THREADS)
SAVE_PREDICTIONS <- FALSE

cat("Threads:", N_THREADS, "\n")
cat("Statistical workers:", STAT_WORKERS, "\n")
cat("Test horizon:", TEST_DAYS, "calendar days\n")
```

# 3. Data preparation

```{r load-data}
train_raw <- read_csv(
  TRAIN_CSV,
  col_types = cols(
    Store = col_integer(),
    DayOfWeek = col_integer(),
    Date = col_date(format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    Sales = col_double(),
    Customers = col_double(),
    Open = col_integer(),
    Promo = col_integer(),
    StateHoliday = col_character(),
    SchoolHoliday = col_integer()
  )
)

store_raw <- read_csv(
  STORE_CSV,
  col_types = cols(
    Store = col_integer(),
    StoreType = col_character(),
    Assortment = col_character(),
    CompetitionDistance = col_double(),
    CompetitionOpenSinceMonth = col_double(),
    CompetitionOpenSinceYear = col_double(),
    Promo2 = col_integer(),
    Promo2SinceWeek = col_double(),
    Promo2SinceYear = col_double(),
    PromoInterval = col_character()
  )
)
```

Sales-history features are constructed on a complete daily calendar. Closed
days are represented by zero sales so that a 42-day lag always means 42
calendar days. Model accuracy is still evaluated only on open days with
positive sales, matching the main thesis analysis.

```{r complete-calendar}
date_range <- seq(min(train_raw$Date), max(train_raw$Date), by = "day")
store_ids <- sort(unique(train_raw$Store))

calendar_sales <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  Store = store_ids,
  Date = date_range
) %>%
  left_join(
    train_raw %>%
      select(Store, Date, Sales, Open, Promo, StateHoliday, SchoolHoliday),
    by = c("Store", "Date")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Open = replace_na(Open, 0L),
    Sales = if_else(Open == 1L, replace_na(Sales, 0), 0),
    Promo = replace_na(Promo, 0L),
    StateHoliday = replace_na(StateHoliday, "0"),
    SchoolHoliday = replace_na(SchoolHoliday, 0L)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Store, Date)
```

```{r origin-safe-history}
add_origin_safe_history <- function(x) {
  x <- x %>% arrange(Date)

  x$lag42 <- dplyr::lag(x$Sales, 42)
  x$lag49 <- dplyr::lag(x$Sales, 49)
  x$lag56 <- dplyr::lag(x$Sales, 56)
  x$lag84 <- dplyr::lag(x$Sales, 84)

  roll7 <- zoo::rollmeanr(x$Sales, 7, fill = NA)
  roll28 <- zoo::rollmeanr(x$Sales, 28, fill = NA)
  x$origin_roll7 <- dplyr::lag(roll7, 42)
  x$origin_roll28 <- dplyr::lag(roll28, 42)

  x
}

calendar_sales <- calendar_sales %>%
  group_by(Store) %>%
  group_modify(~ add_origin_safe_history(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r model-frame}
df <- calendar_sales %>%
  left_join(store_raw, by = "Store") %>%
  mutate(
    DayOfWeek = wday(Date, week_start = 1),
    Year = year(Date),
    Month = month(Date),
    Week = isoweek(Date),
    DayOfMonth = mday(Date),
    Quarter = quarter(Date),
    IsWeekend = as.integer(DayOfWeek %in% c(6, 7)),
    ForecastTrend = as.integer(Date - min(Date)),
    StateHoliday = case_when(
      StateHoliday == "0" ~ 0L,
      StateHoliday == "a" ~ 1L,
      StateHoliday == "b" ~ 2L,
      StateHoliday == "c" ~ 3L,
      TRUE ~ 0L
    ),
    StoreType = as.integer(factor(StoreType, levels = c("a", "b", "c", "d"))),
    Assortment = as.integer(factor(Assortment, levels = c("a", "b", "c"))),
    CompetitionOpenMonths = if_else(
      !is.na(CompetitionOpenSinceYear) &
        !is.na(CompetitionOpenSinceMonth),
      (Year - CompetitionOpenSinceYear) * 12 +
        (Month - CompetitionOpenSinceMonth),
      0
    ),
    CompetitionOpenMonths = pmax(CompetitionOpenMonths, 0),
    CompetitionDistance = replace_na(
      CompetitionDistance,
      median(CompetitionDistance, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    Promo2 = replace_na(Promo2, 0L)
  ) %>%
  filter(Open == 1L, Sales > 0) %>%
  arrange(Date, Store)

all_dates <- sort(unique(df$Date))
test_start <- all_dates[length(all_dates) - TEST_DAYS + 1L]
test_end <- max(all_dates)
forecast_origin <- test_start - days(1)

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Horizon = if_else(
      Date >= test_start,
      as.integer(Date - forecast_origin),
      0L
    )
  )

cat("Open-day rows:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Stores:", n_distinct(df$Store), "\n")
cat("Forecast origin:", as.character(forecast_origin), "\n")
cat("Test period:", as.character(test_start), "to", as.character(test_end), "\n")
```

# 4. Incremental information sets

The first feature set approximates an old-M-style information environment:
the model receives only store identity and lagged summaries of the store's own
sales history. The other feature sets add groups of information while retaining
all earlier features.

```{r feature-sets}
HISTORY_FEATURES <- c(
  "Store",
  "lag42", "lag49", "lag56", "lag84",
  "origin_roll7", "origin_roll28"
)

CALENDAR_FEATURES <- c(
  "DayOfWeek", "Month", "Week", "DayOfMonth",
  "Quarter", "IsWeekend", "Year", "ForecastTrend"
)

STORE_FEATURES <- c(
  "StoreType", "Assortment",
  "CompetitionDistance", "CompetitionOpenMonths"
)

COMMERCIAL_FEATURES <- c(
  "Promo", "Promo2", "StateHoliday", "SchoolHoliday"
)

FEATURE_STAGES <- list(
  "1 History only" = HISTORY_FEATURES,
  "2 + Calendar" = c(HISTORY_FEATURES, CALENDAR_FEATURES),
  "3 + Store attributes" = c(
    HISTORY_FEATURES, CALENDAR_FEATURES, STORE_FEATURES
  ),
  "4 + Promotions and holidays" = c(
    HISTORY_FEATURES, CALENDAR_FEATURES,
    STORE_FEATURES, COMMERCIAL_FEATURES
  )
)

feature_stage_table <- imap_dfr(
  FEATURE_STAGES,
  ~ tibble(
    Stage = .y,
    N_features = length(.x),
    Features = paste(.x, collapse = ", ")
  )
)

print(feature_stage_table, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

# 5. Split, metrics, and validation helpers

```{r helpers}
rmse <- function(actual, pred) sqrt(mean((actual - pred)^2))
mae <- function(actual, pred) mean(abs(actual - pred))
mape <- function(actual, pred) {
  valid <- !is.na(actual) & actual != 0
  mean(abs((actual[valid] - pred[valid]) / actual[valid])) * 100
}
r2_test <- function(actual, pred) {
  denom <- sum((actual - mean(actual))^2)
  if (denom == 0) return(NA_real_)
  1 - sum((actual - pred)^2) / denom
}
improvement <- function(reference_rmse, model_rmse) {
  100 * (reference_rmse - model_rmse) / reference_rmse
}
evaluate <- function(actual, pred) {
  tibble(
    RMSE = rmse(actual, pred),
    MAE = mae(actual, pred),
    MAPE = mape(actual, pred),
    R2_test = r2_test(actual, pred)
  )
}

make_split <- function(data, features) {
  required <- c(features, "Sales", "Date", "Store", "DayOfWeek")
  clean <- data %>%
    filter(if_all(all_of(features), ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
    arrange(Date, Store)

  train <- clean %>% filter(Date < test_start)
  test <- clean %>% filter(Date >= test_start, Date <= test_end)

  list(
    train = train,
    test = test,
    X_train = as.matrix(train[, features]),
    y_train = train$Sales,
    X_test = as.matrix(test[, features]),
    y_test = test$Sales
  )
}

make_temporal_folds <- function(data, k = CV_FOLDS) {
  dates <- sort(unique(data$Date))
  boundaries <- floor(seq(
    length(dates) / (k + 1),
    length(dates) * k / (k + 1),
    length.out = k
  ))

  lapply(boundaries, function(boundary) {
    train_dates <- dates[seq_len(boundary)]
    val_end <- min(length(dates), boundary + floor(length(dates) / (k + 1)))
    val_dates <- dates[(boundary + 1L):val_end]
    list(
      train = which(data$Date %in% train_dates),
      val = which(data$Date %in% val_dates)
    )
  })
}
```

# 6. Benchmarks

Store-mean and Store-DOW are recalculated on the same modelling sample used by
the feature stages. Auto-ARIMA, ETS, and Theta are fitted once on the common
primary holdout because their information set does not change across the ML
stages.

```{r simple-benchmarks}
benchmark_split <- make_split(df, FEATURE_STAGES[[1]])
benchmark_train <- df %>% filter(Date < test_start)

store_mean_lookup <- benchmark_train %>%
  group_by(Store) %>%
  summarise(Prediction = mean(Sales), .groups = "drop")

store_dow_lookup <- benchmark_train %>%
  group_by(Store, DayOfWeek) %>%
  summarise(Prediction = mean(Sales), .groups = "drop")

store_fallback <- benchmark_train %>%
  group_by(Store) %>%
  summarise(StoreMean = mean(Sales), .groups = "drop")

global_mean <- mean(benchmark_train$Sales)

pred_store_mean <- benchmark_split$test %>%
  left_join(store_mean_lookup, by = "Store") %>%
  mutate(Prediction = replace_na(Prediction, global_mean)) %>%
  pull(Prediction)

pred_store_dow <- benchmark_split$test %>%
  left_join(store_dow_lookup, by = c("Store", "DayOfWeek")) %>%
  left_join(store_fallback, by = "Store") %>%
  mutate(Prediction = coalesce(Prediction, StoreMean, global_mean)) %>%
  pull(Prediction)

simple_benchmarks <- bind_rows(
  evaluate(benchmark_split$y_test, pred_store_mean) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Store-mean", .before = 1),
  evaluate(benchmark_split$y_test, pred_store_dow) %>%
    mutate(Model = "Store-DOW", .before = 1)
)

print(simple_benchmarks)
```

```{r statistical-benchmarks}
run_statistical_benchmarks <- function(train_daily, test_open,
                                       workers = STAT_WORKERS) {
  horizon <- as.integer(test_end - forecast_origin)
  stores <- sort(unique(test_open$Store))

  fit_one_store <- function(store_id) {
    observed <- train_daily %>%
      filter(Store == store_id, Date <= forecast_origin) %>%
      select(Date, Sales)

    complete <- tibble(
      Date = seq(min(observed$Date), forecast_origin, by = "day")
    ) %>%
      left_join(observed, by = "Date") %>%
      mutate(Sales = replace_na(Sales, 0))

    y <- ts(complete$Sales, frequency = 7)

    safe_fit <- function(expr) {
      tryCatch(
        as.numeric(expr),
        error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, horizon)
      )
    }

    arima_pred <- safe_fit(
      forecast(
        auto.arima(
          y,
          seasonal = TRUE,
          stepwise = TRUE,
          approximation = TRUE,
          max.p = 3, max.q = 3,
          max.P = 1, max.Q = 1,
          max.order = 5
        ),
        h = horizon
      )$mean
    )
    ets_pred <- safe_fit(forecast(ets(y), h = horizon)$mean)
    theta_pred <- safe_fit(thetaf(y, h = horizon)$mean)

    forecast_tbl <- tibble(
      Store = store_id,
      Date = seq(test_start, test_end, by = "day"),
      ARIMA = pmax(0, arima_pred),
      ETS = pmax(0, ets_pred),
      Theta = pmax(0, theta_pred)
    )

    test_open %>%
      filter(Store == store_id) %>%
      select(Store, Date, Sales) %>%
      left_join(forecast_tbl, by = c("Store", "Date"))
  }

  parts <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "unix" && workers > 1L) {
    parallel::mclapply(
      stores, fit_one_store,
      mc.cores = workers,
      mc.preschedule = TRUE
    )
  } else {
    lapply(stores, fit_one_store)
  }

  predictions <- bind_rows(parts)

  if (anyNA(predictions[, c("ARIMA", "ETS", "Theta")])) {
    stop("At least one statistical model failed. Inspect predictions.")
  }

  metrics <- map_dfr(c("ARIMA", "ETS", "Theta"), function(model) {
    evaluate(predictions$Sales, predictions[[model]]) %>%
      mutate(Model = model, .before = 1)
  })

  list(metrics = metrics, predictions = predictions)
}

statistical_obj <- run_statistical_benchmarks(
  train_daily = calendar_sales,
  test_open = benchmark_split$test
)
statistical_benchmarks <- statistical_obj$metrics
print(statistical_benchmarks)
```

```{r benchmark-summary}
all_benchmarks <- bind_rows(simple_benchmarks, statistical_benchmarks) %>%
  arrange(RMSE)

best_statistical <- statistical_benchmarks %>%
  slice_min(RMSE, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

store_dow_rmse <- simple_benchmarks$RMSE[
  simple_benchmarks$Model == "Store-DOW"
]
best_stat_rmse <- best_statistical$RMSE
best_stat_name <- best_statistical$Model

cat("Best statistical benchmark:", best_stat_name, "\n")
print(all_benchmarks, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

# 7. XGBoost and LightGBM

```{r boosted-functions-v2}
xgb_train_with_validation <- function(params, data, nrounds, validation,
                                      early_stopping_rounds, verbose = 0) {
  train_args <- list(
    params = params,
    data = data,
    nrounds = nrounds,
    early_stopping_rounds = early_stopping_rounds,
    verbose = verbose
  )

  # xgboost < 2 uses `watchlist`; newer releases renamed it to `evals`.
  if ("evals" %in% names(formals(xgboost::xgb.train))) {
    train_args$evals <- list(validation = validation)
  } else {
    train_args$watchlist <- list(validation = validation)
  }

  do.call(xgboost::xgb.train, train_args)
}

run_xgboost <- function(split, seed = 42) {
  folds <- make_temporal_folds(split$train)

  best_rounds <- map_int(folds, function(fold) {
    dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(
      split$X_train[fold$train, , drop = FALSE],
      label = split$y_train[fold$train]
    )
    dval <- xgb.DMatrix(
      split$X_train[fold$val, , drop = FALSE],
      label = split$y_train[fold$val]
    )

    fit <- xgb_train_with_validation(
      params = list(
        objective = "reg:squarederror",
        eta = 0.1,
        max_depth = 6,
        subsample = 0.8,
        colsample_bytree = 0.8,
        nthread = N_THREADS,
        seed = seed,
        verbosity = 0
      ),
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = XGB_MAX_ROUNDS,
      validation = dval,
      early_stopping_rounds = XGB_EARLY_STOP,
      verbose = 0
    )
    if (length(fit$best_iteration) == 0L || is.na(fit$best_iteration)) {
      XGB_MAX_ROUNDS
    } else {
      fit$best_iteration
    }
  })

  final_rounds <- round(mean(best_rounds))
  dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(split$X_train, label = split$y_train)
  dtest <- xgb.DMatrix(split$X_test)

  fit <- xgb.train(
    params = list(
      objective = "reg:squarederror",
      eta = 0.1,
      max_depth = 6,
      subsample = 0.8,
      colsample_bytree = 0.8,
      nthread = N_THREADS,
      seed = seed,
      verbosity = 0
    ),
    data = dtrain,
    nrounds = final_rounds,
    verbose = 0
  )

  pred <- predict(fit, dtest)
  list(
    metrics = evaluate(split$y_test, pred),
    model = fit,
    predictions = pred,
    rounds = final_rounds
  )
}

run_lightgbm <- function(split, seed = 42) {
  folds <- make_temporal_folds(split$train)

  best_rounds <- map_int(folds, function(fold) {
    dtrain <- lgb.Dataset(
      split$X_train[fold$train, , drop = FALSE],
      label = split$y_train[fold$train]
    )
    dval <- lgb.Dataset(
      split$X_train[fold$val, , drop = FALSE],
      label = split$y_train[fold$val]
    )

    fit <- lgb.train(
      params = list(
        objective = "regression",
        metric = "rmse",
        num_leaves = 63,
        learning_rate = 0.05,
        bagging_fraction = 0.8,
        bagging_freq = 1,
        feature_fraction = 0.8,
        num_threads = N_THREADS,
        seed = seed,
        bagging_seed = seed,
        feature_fraction_seed = seed,
        verbosity = -1
      ),
      data = dtrain,
      nrounds = LGB_MAX_ROUNDS,
      valids = list(validation = dval),
      early_stopping_rounds = LGB_EARLY_STOP,
      verbose = -1
    )
    if (length(fit$best_iter) == 0L ||
        is.na(fit$best_iter) ||
        fit$best_iter <= 0L) {
      LGB_MAX_ROUNDS
    } else {
      fit$best_iter
    }
  })

  final_rounds <- round(mean(best_rounds))
  dtrain <- lgb.Dataset(split$X_train, label = split$y_train)

  fit <- lgb.train(
    params = list(
      objective = "regression",
      metric = "rmse",
      num_leaves = 63,
      learning_rate = 0.05,
      bagging_fraction = 0.8,
      bagging_freq = 1,
      feature_fraction = 0.8,
      num_threads = N_THREADS,
      seed = seed,
      bagging_seed = seed,
      feature_fraction_seed = seed,
      verbosity = -1
    ),
    data = dtrain,
    nrounds = final_rounds,
    verbose = -1
  )

  pred <- predict(fit, split$X_test)
  list(
    metrics = evaluate(split$y_test, pred),
    model = fit,
    predictions = pred,
    rounds = final_rounds
  )
}
```

# 8. Incremental feature experiment

```{r run-feature-stages-v2}
stage_objects <- list()

stage_results <- imap_dfr(FEATURE_STAGES, function(features, stage_name) {
  cat("\nRunning:", stage_name, "\n")
  split <- make_split(df, features)

  xgb_obj <- run_xgboost(split, seed = 42)
  lgb_obj <- run_lightgbm(split, seed = 42)

  stage_objects[[stage_name]] <<- list(
    split = split,
    XGBoost = xgb_obj,
    LightGBM = lgb_obj,
    features = features
  )

  bind_rows(
    xgb_obj$metrics %>%
      mutate(Model = "XGBoost", Rounds = xgb_obj$rounds, .before = 1),
    lgb_obj$metrics %>%
      mutate(Model = "LightGBM", Rounds = lgb_obj$rounds, .before = 1)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Stage = stage_name,
      N_features = length(features),
      N_train = nrow(split$train),
      N_test = nrow(split$test),
      .before = 1
    )
})

stage_results <- stage_results %>%
  mutate(
    Improvement_vs_StoreDOW = improvement(store_dow_rmse, RMSE),
    Improvement_vs_BestStat = improvement(best_stat_rmse, RMSE),
    Beats_StoreDOW = RMSE < store_dow_rmse,
    Beats_BestStat = RMSE < best_stat_rmse
  )

print(stage_results, n = Inf, width = Inf)

stage_predictions <- imap_dfr(stage_objects, function(objects, stage_name) {
  bind_rows(
    objects$split$test %>%
      transmute(
        Stage = stage_name,
        Model = "XGBoost",
        Store, Date, Actual = Sales,
        Prediction = objects$XGBoost$predictions
      ),
    objects$split$test %>%
      transmute(
        Stage = stage_name,
        Model = "LightGBM",
        Store, Date, Actual = Sales,
        Prediction = objects$LightGBM$predictions
      )
  )
})
```

# 9. When does machine learning overtake the benchmarks?

```{r transition-analysis}
stage_levels <- names(FEATURE_STAGES)

transition_table <- stage_results %>%
  mutate(Stage = factor(Stage, levels = stage_levels)) %>%
  arrange(Model, Stage) %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  summarise(
    First_stage_beating_StoreDOW = if (any(Beats_StoreDOW)) {
      as.character(Stage[which(Beats_StoreDOW)[1]])
    } else {
      "Never"
    },
    First_stage_beating_best_statistical = if (any(Beats_BestStat)) {
      as.character(Stage[which(Beats_BestStat)[1]])
    } else {
      "Never"
    },
    Best_stage = as.character(Stage[which.min(RMSE)]),
    Best_RMSE = min(RMSE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("\nBest statistical model:", best_stat_name,
    "with RMSE", round(best_stat_rmse, 1), "\n")
print(transition_table, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

```{r incremental-gains}
incremental_results <- stage_results %>%
  mutate(Stage = factor(Stage, levels = stage_levels)) %>%
  arrange(Model, Stage) %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  mutate(
    Previous_RMSE = lag(RMSE),
    Incremental_RMSE_reduction = Previous_RMSE - RMSE,
    Incremental_improvement_pct = 100 *
      (Previous_RMSE - RMSE) / Previous_RMSE
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

print(
  incremental_results %>%
    select(
      Stage, Model, RMSE, Previous_RMSE,
      Incremental_RMSE_reduction, Incremental_improvement_pct,
      Beats_StoreDOW, Beats_BestStat
    ),
  n = Inf,
  width = Inf
)
```

# 10. Visual results

```{r plot-rmse-path, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
benchmark_lines <- tibble(

    title = "When does machine learning overtake the benchmarks?",

      "Fixed-origin 42-day forecasts; best statistical benchmark is ",

    ),

    y = "RMSE",
    colour = NULL,
    linetype = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

# 11. Feature importance in the final specification

```{r final-importance}
final_stage <- tail(stage_levels, 1)
final_obj <- stage_objects[[final_stage]]

xgb_importance <- xgb.importance(
  feature_names = final_obj$features,
  model = final_obj$XGBoost$model
) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  transmute(Feature, Gain, Model = "XGBoost")

lgb_importance <- lgb.importance(final_obj$LightGBM$model) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  transmute(Feature, Gain, Model = "LightGBM")

importance_all <- bind_rows(xgb_importance, lgb_importance) %>%
  mutate(
    InformationGroup = case_when(
      Feature %in% HISTORY_FEATURES ~ "Sales history",
      Feature %in% CALENDAR_FEATURES ~ "Calendar",
      Feature %in% STORE_FEATURES ~ "Store/competition",
      Feature %in% COMMERCIAL_FEATURES ~ "Promotion/holiday",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )

importance_groups <- importance_all %>%
  group_by(Model, InformationGroup) %>%
  summarise(Gain = sum(Gain), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  mutate(GainShare = Gain / sum(Gain)) %>%
  ungroup()

print(importance_groups, n = Inf, width = Inf)
```

```{r plot-importance-groups, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
p_importance_groups <- importance_groups %>%
  ggplot(aes(InformationGroup, GainShare * 100, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "XGBoost" = "#3F82E0",
    "LightGBM" = "#E96B5F"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Information used by the final ML specifications",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Share of total gain importance (%)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

p_importance_groups
```

# 12. Direct interpretation

```{r automatic-interpretation, results='asis'}
cat("## Automatic answer\n\n")

walk(seq_len(nrow(transition_table)), function(i) {
  row <- transition_table[i, ]
  cat(
    "**", row$Model, "** first beats Store-DOW at **",
    row$First_stage_beating_StoreDOW,
    "** and first beats the best statistical model (",
    best_stat_name, ") at **",
    row$First_stage_beating_best_statistical,
    "**. Its lowest RMSE is ",
    round(row$Best_RMSE, 1),
    " at **", row$Best_stage, "**.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )
})

largest_additions <- incremental_results %>%
  filter(!is.na(Incremental_improvement_pct)) %>%
  group_by(Model) %>%
  slice_max(Incremental_improvement_pct, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

walk(seq_len(nrow(largest_additions)), function(i) {
  row <- largest_additions[i, ]
  cat(
    "The largest incremental improvement for **", row$Model,
    "** occurs at **", as.character(row$Stage),
    "**, reducing RMSE by ",
    sprintf("%.1f", row$Incremental_improvement_pct),
    "\\% relative to the preceding information set.\n\n",
    sep = ""
  )
})
```
